tldr_label: TL;DR — The Nasdaq has its worst day since April 2025, Asia follows, and Trump blames Democrats

tldr_bullets.label: Wall Street
tldr_bullets.body: The Nasdaq fell 5.5% into correction territory and the S&P 500 lost 4.4% as AI and chip stocks collapsed, erasing Wednesday's rally. [[TAG:danger:Nasdaq -5.5%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Asia
tldr_bullets.body: Bloomberg and Fox Business reported that Japan's Nikkei entered a bear market and that Korea's Kospi and Taiwan's Taiex plunged on Friday. [[TAG:danger:Nikkei bear market]]

tldr_bullets.label: Jobs
tldr_bullets.body: October payrolls, due today, are expected to show about 65,000 new jobs. Traders are weighing a Fed hike in December.

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Herzog says 67 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot and will hand over the mandate on Sunday. CNN reported he called Trump's plan to end annual military aid 'a bolt from the blue'.

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump is weighing whether to resume the war as US Central Command prepares options. Iran says talks are 'proceeding very intensively'.

tldr_bullets.label: World
tldr_bullets.body: More than 600,000 marched in France. The toll from the Zaporizhzhia aid-center strike has risen to about 42, and early results show the ANC near 32% in South Africa.

sections.title: AI Meltdown
sections.summary: Nasdaq posts its worst day since April 2025 as chip stocks crash; Trump blames Democrats

paragraphs.heading: The rout
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Nvidia and Qualcomm fell more than 9%, pushing the Nasdaq to its worst day since April 2025. The Motley Fool said the AI trade came under fire. StockTitan reported a sharply lower close as the chip selloff spread, and Yahoo Finance said the Dow lost about 1,800 points as the Nasdaq entered a correction. Reported closes are Nasdaq down 5.5%, S&P 500 down 4.4% and Dow down 3.4%. [[TAG:danger:S&P -4.4%]]

paragraphs.heading: Why
paragraphs.body: CNBC tied part of the selloff to Qualcomm's weak outlook. Reuters, via The Globe and Mail, cited fears that Democratic control of Congress could slow the buildout of AI data centers. Fox Business reported that Trump blamed the 'Dumocrats' for the drop. Analysts point mainly to worries about AI spending and crowded positions, and Business Standard also carried Trump's claim.

paragraphs.heading: Asia and today
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg and Fox Business reported that Asian markets plunged on Friday. The Nikkei fell into a bear market and Korea's Kospi dropped more than 6% after a trading halt. The Globe and Mail said Nasdaq futures rose early as chip stocks stabilized. Kiplinger and FXStreet said the October jobs report is due, with about 65,000 jobs expected.

sections.summary: Trump weighs resuming the war as CENTCOM prepares options; Tehran says talks are intensive

paragraphs.heading: Next move
paragraphs.body: Fox News reported that Trump met his national security team as US Central Command prepares for possible strikes. PBS said Trump must now weigh his next move in a war that contributed to the Republican defeat. CBS News reported more attacks on ships in the Gulf, and that Iran says talks through mediators are 'proceeding very intensively' and that the outcome depends on Washington. sections.title: Israel
sections.summary: 67 lawmakers back Eisenkot, with the mandate due Sunday; Trump's aid cut stuns Jerusalem

paragraphs.heading: Mandate
paragraphs.body: JNS and the Times of Israel reported Herzog saying that factions with 67 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot and 46 backed Netanyahu, and that he will assign the mandate on Sunday. Ynet said Eisenkot is close to the mandate. Herzog warned that 'mutual vetoes' between and within the blocs leave the outcome open, and 19 of the 67 recommendations come from Arab-led parties. [[TAG:info:mandate Sunday]]

paragraphs.heading: Aid shock
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that Herzog called Trump's announcement ending annual US military aid 'like a bolt from the blue'. The Washington Post and Fox News reported that Trump said the roughly $4 billion a year would end by the close of 2026, while Israel could still buy weapons. It is unclear how this squares with the existing aid agreement, which runs to 2028. [[TAG:warning:details unclear]]

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Aid-center toll climbs past 40 with dozens missing; Trump says a deal is near

paragraphs.heading: Toll
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that the toll from Russia's strike on the aid site in Komyshuvakha reached 40, with dozens still missing. The Oman Observer reported 42, and The Insider had earlier reported 31. Russia says it hit Ukrainian troops. [[TAG:danger:40+ killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Diplomacy
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Trump said a Russia-Ukraine deal is near after meeting Putin's envoy, though he gave no specifics. NBC News said a US envoy called the renewed security talks productive as the two sides traded airstrikes.

sections.title: France in the Streets
sections.summary: Biggest protest day in years as unions and students march over wages and costs

paragraphs.heading: Turnout
paragraphs.body: CNN called it France's biggest day of protests in years. CP24 reported that more than 600,000 people rallied, according to the interior ministry, while the CGT union claimed nearly 1.6 million. The Washington Post said the crowds demanded higher wages and backed students' demands. The day was largely peaceful, with some local clashes, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has called a 'social conference' with unions and employers for November 9. [[TAG:warning:600K+ marched]]

sections.title: Votes Still Counting
sections.summary: Alaska's Senate race stays tight; South Africa's ANC near 32% with results due Sunday

paragraphs.heading: Alaska
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post reported that Mary Peltola narrowly leads Senator Dan Sullivan, and The Hill reported the same narrow lead. The Anchorage Daily News tracked the early count. Alaska counts ballots by ranked choice, and the race had not been called in these reports.

paragraphs.heading: South Africa
paragraphs.body: The Citizen said early results do not look promising for the ANC. Swisher Post, citing the electoral commission's dashboard, reported the ANC at about 32% and leading in 62 councils with roughly 69% counted. MyBroadband said the DA may fall short in Johannesburg and Pretoria as ActionSA gains. Official results are due on Sunday. [[TAG:info:results Sunday]]
